claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a homogeneous high-temperature BCC initial state.
The high-temperature BCC state lies close to a multiphase boundary in the thermodynamic free-energy landscape.
Diffusion during cooling or thermal exposure produces slight local compositional changes.
Cooling or thermal exposure produces local ordering changes.
Small local compositional and ordering changes can shift the local free-energy minimum.
Shifts in the local free-energy minimum can trigger nucleation of secondary phases.
B2 and L12 are examples of nearly degenerate phases relevant to the proposed local free-energy shifts.
Cooling rate modulates local compositional and ordering changes and thereby governs secondary-phase nucleation and growth kinetics.
Aging time modulates local compositional and ordering changes and thereby governs secondary-phase nucleation and growth kinetics.
Slow cooling or aging at 600–800 °C provides sufficient diffusion for local composition and ordering to evolve.
Ultra-rapid quenching suppresses diffusion sufficiently to prevent the proposed local free-energy adjustments.
Preventing local free-energy adjustments under ultra-rapid quenching will suppress secondary-phase nucleation through the proposed mechanism.
Changing cooling rate or hold time will systematically change the fractions of emerging phases relative to a moderate-cooling baseline.
Changing cooling rate or hold time will systematically change the onset times of emerging phases relative to a moderate-cooling baseline.
Diffraction peak positions and intensities will evolve in a manner corresponding to changing phase volume fractions.
The measured phase evolution will align with CALPHAD-predicted free-energy changes.
A moderate cooling rate yields phase evolution consistent with current CALPHAD predictions for the BCC state without strong diffusion effects.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as moderate cooling without strong diffusion effects, while the applicability conditions identify intermediate or moderate cooling regimes as those permitting the active diffusion required by the mechanism. The diffusion state of the baseline is therefore internally ambiguous.
